author: Mary Ann Castillo
title: Ask a Foodie: The Great Redhawk Showdown - basketball vs. baseball edi...
text:
One question I’m asked often is: “What do you do if you don’t like the food?” Today’s column is brought to you by a failed surf and turf dish. It had rave reviews, and all the ingredients were ones I adore. The idea of them combined on one plate sounded like perfection. Wrong.
The restaurant was busy. They forgot about my order. A kind server — not mine — noticed I’d been waiting and jumped into action (my hero). Minutes later, my dish arrived. It looked and smelled fantastic. The portion was generous. The first bite of shrimp? Amazing.
But as I kept eating, the salt overwhelmed everything. I tried to rationalize: maybe it was the blackened seasoning … maybe the combination of ingredients … maybe they took the “surf” part seriously and sautéed the toppings with sand to mimic gulping ocean water after being wiped out by a wave. Eventually, I had to poke fun at myself: “Maybe someone blessed your food with a handful of salt?”
I weighed my options. I’d already eaten and paid. Should I return later that week to give them a second chance or move on?
I’m OK with others disagreeing with me, but I won’t mislead readers about my experiences. That day, it wasn’t good. I own my part. When the food took too long, I could’ve followed up. When the helpful server asked how it was, I could’ve mentioned the extreme saltiness. I did neither. Why? Because in the grand scheme of things, it wasn’t a big deal.
And that’s how I ended up at Mary Jane Bourbon + Smokehouse for lunch.
According to their Facebook page, the return of SEMO students kicked off a friendly fried bologna sandwich contest between SEMO Basketball Coach Briley Palmer and SEMO Baseball Coach Andy Sawyers.
Each of their sandwiches was added to the menu for August, giving the community time to weigh in.
Ladies first: The Mrs. Coach Palmer.
Coach Palmer went with a traditional approach and amped it up with a special ingredient. Her sandwich featured two thick slices of white bread, mayo, cheese — and then the kicker: chips inside the sandwich. Yes, inside! The downhome secret “sauce” of any homemade white bread sandwich. Even better, large toothpicks suspended the top bread above the chips, keeping them crisp until the moment of delicious crunch, where the magic truly lives.
The competition: The Sawdawg.
Coach Sawyers took a creative angle on the classic. His version included the usual suspects — fried bologna, American cheese, a thick slice of onion — and added a favorite of gourmands everywhere: garlic aioli. It was a bold move.
To keep it fair, I brought in two coworkers as unbiased referees.
Unlike the beautiful (and possibly sinister) sideline presence of Coach Palmer, her sandwich wasn’t winning any beauty contests. And the name, “Mrs. Coach Palmer”, didn’t exactly scream originality. While I loved seeing chips in the sandwich, I did worry about choking down all that bread.
The Sawdawg, on the other hand, had a fun name, melty cheese, and the onion and bologna peeked temptingly from a golden bun. “Aioli” always feels a bit fancy — even when it’s just gourmet mayo.
The verdict?
Coach Palmer dominated this round. Coach Sawyers didn’t even get on the scoreboard.
Maybe it was female instinct, or maybe it was nostalgia. Either way, everyone voted for the Mrs. Coach Palmer sandwich. It brought comfort. Whether you’re a freshman far from home or a 51-year-old decades removed from sack lunches, sometimes there’s just nothing better than a classic fried bologna sandwich to ease a bout of homesickness.
Whether you’re a diehard bologna lover or a rowdy Redhawk, you still have a little more than 10 days to join the fun and weigh in on the challenge at Mary Jane Bourbon + Smokehouse located at 1107 Broadway in Cape Girardeau.
Mary Ann Castillo has more than 50 years of eating experience with no plans to stop.
